code.note: Fortran shar archive. Remove everything above the #! /bin/sh line (or extract its shar members with sh), giving Drivers/driver.f (program TOMS344_PRB calling test01), Src/src.f (subroutine TTEST), Sp/ and a Makefile, plus the shipped output file res. Build driver.f with src.f and run it; the claim is on the printed table, row 1.

claim.location: The shipped reference output res (member of 344.gz). Row 1 of the table after the header 'DF X CDF computed' is DF=1, X=0.3250, computed CDF 0.7999537587165833. The exact column in the same row is 0.7999538183212280.

reference.file: res (member of 344.gz), row DF=1 X=0.3250, computed column

claim.metric: The CDF value printed by TOMS344_PRB for DF=1, X=0.3250 (the TTEST result, the 'CDF computed' column), compared with 0.7999537587165833 from res.
claim.paper_value: Not used: the paper is paywalled and was not read.

values.name: TTEST, DF=1, X=0.3250, two-tailed CDF transform (computed column)

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The shipped computed value differs from the exact Mathematica value in the same row by 6e-8, and single-precision REAL arithmetic in the code gives errors of that order. 1e-6 absolute is about 16 times that row's shipped deviation from exact and leaves room for compiler and libm differences in the last digits. Not to be loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 minute: one Fortran compile and a run over 14 table rows.
cost.data_licence: Netlib TOMS code under the ACM licence; the rerun should record the licence text.

why: TTEST is a short Fortran evaluation of the Student t CDF with a shipped table of computed values, so the claim is a checkable number the code must compute.
